verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna as the two stand on the battlefield. Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt and grief, unable to lift his bow. Krishna is telling him to act, to fight, without clinging to what will happen next. The verse says that no sincere effort ever goes to waste. Even a small amount of this practice, this giving yourself fully to your part while letting go of the result, protects you from great fear.
verse.for_you: You quit your job and put everything into this brand. That is the work. The fear you feel is the old life fading. Keep going. Your effort is already shielding you.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is teaching the young Rama that the world is not ruled by some hidden force. He says that what people call fate is only the result of past effort. The fruit of your work comes sooner or later, depending on the time and the place. Your present effort shapes tomorrow, so do not grieve over what was never in your hands.
verse.for_you: You have left the safety of a job to build something yours. Today, let the quiet moments remind you that your effort is already shaping tomorrow, even if the results are not here yet.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from a place of steady resolve. He tells them that praise and blame from others, the coming and going of money, and the timing of death are all passing things. What matters is the path of what is right. The steady do not move a step from it no matter what happens. He says setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path. This is the truth underneath your own early days.
verse.for_you: Your work right now is to keep going on the path you chose when you quit your job. The money has not come yet, and people will talk. Let them praise or blame. Stay on the path. The steady do not step off it.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi, who has lost her kingdom, stands in the forest and questions Yudhishthira, the eldest, about why the righteous suffer. She asks how he can keep his faith when his effort has led only to exile and loss. Yudhishthira answers that he acts because it is right, not for reward, and that effort still matters. The verse tells us that every attempt can end in success or not, and only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.for_you: Some mornings the work will feel like a gamble with no prize. That is the test. Do what you do because it is yours, not because the next sale is already in the bag.

verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.

story.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

script: You just stepped off a path that was not yours and you are breathing hard in the open air. That is a real thing. You are alive and you are determined and nothing is wrong with that.

Arjuna stands on the battlefield, his famous bow resting on the ground. The man he must fight is his own teacher. He is paralyzed by grief and doubt. He cannot lift his weapon. And Krishna, his charioteer and guide, looks at him and says: And Krishna replied:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते, स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्.
In plain words: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.

This is the yoga of action. It means you give yourself fully to your part and you let go of owning the result. No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear. This is easier said than done, because every morning you will want to know if it is working. But the fear you feel is not a sign to stop. It is the old life fading. The protection is already there.
Your part is building the brand. The result is not yours to own today. Do the work fully. Let the fear be the proof that you are stepping into what is yours.
The old life is fading. What remains is yours.

depth.life: You quit your job last week and built a brand with nothing in the bank. You feel more alive than ever, and the work is still exciting. But the phone is in your hand seven hours a day, and the novelty is wearing thin.
depth.points: Krishna tells Arjuna that no sincere effort is ever wasted. The work itself is the protection. The fear is not of failure, but of the old life fading away.
depth.practice: Put the phone down for the first hour of your morning. Let your mind rest before it reaches for the next notification.
depth.question: What does your work feel like when it is not trying to prove anything to the world?
